how: Grants, loans and free help a local church can use, found for v10.58.0 on the official pages of the bodies that run them (each with a quote checked word for word); read on 7 Oct 2026. Not here: scholarships for one member, and what initiatives.json already lists (Frame websites, the Discover Bible School through the Discovery Centers). Versacare is an Adventist foundation, listed with the division-wide items.

items.name: ACS Seed Grant
items.years: Portal opens on set dates; next date 26 October 2026 (opens 12 pm Eastern for 3 hours)

aims.text: Pays up to 75% (max $10,000) of equipment or supply costs to start or improve a church-based community service (ACS) ministry, such as food pantry fridges, shelving or computers.

localChurch: Talk first with your conference ACS director; the application needs endorsement letters from the ACS director and a conference administrator.
NAD pays up to 75% (max $10,000); your church and conference together cover at least 25%. Capital items only: no salaries, rent, utilities, labor or permits.
Portal open 26 Oct 2026 for 3 hours; money goes through the conference; report due within 6 months; a funded program can apply again after 3 full years.

resources.title: Seed Grant page (dates, template, portal link)

sources.title: ACS Grants Program
sources.quote: Covers 75% (up to $10,000) of capital improvement costs for new or existing ACS centers. Church based ministries may apply in partnership with their Conference ACS Director.

sources.title: ACS Seed Grant
sources.quote: The portal will open at 12 pm Eastern time for 3 hours on these dates above for 2026.

sources.title: Seed Grant Application Requirements (PDF)
sources.quote: Eligible ACS programs must be a church-based ministry associated with one or more local Adventist churches.

items.name: ACS Thrift Store Investment Fund (no-interest loan)
items.years: Applications reviewed as they come in (no deadline)

aims.text: A 0% loan of up to $20,000 to open a new church thrift store or grow an existing one as an ACS ministry.

localChurch: Loans up to $20,000 at 0% interest with no collateral.
Fill in the Thrift Store Financial Worksheet and get recommendation letters from your conference ACS director and one other conference administrator.
If approved, NAD ACS, the conference and the church sign an agreement; the check goes to the conference to pass on.

sources.title: ACS Grants Program
sources.quote: The ACS Thrift Investment Fund loans up to $20,000 for starting or expanding church-based ACS thrift store ministries.

sources.title: Thrift Store Investment Fund
sources.quote: Stores may request loans of up to $20,000. The loans are 0% interest and require no collateral.

items.name: NAD Church Revitalization Funding
items.years: No deadline posted; the online application form was open on 7 Oct 2026

aims.text: $3,000 to help a church start a revitalization journey, shared equally by the NAD, the union and the conference.

localChurch: $3,000 per church: $1,000 each from the NAD, your union and your conference.
Church board votes a revitalization plan and runs a church-health check (eAdventist Church Vitality tool, NCD, or one agreed with the conference revitalization coordinator).
Must send a leadership team (pastor plus elders) to an NAD Church Revitalization BootCamp; then apply on the NAD online form.

sources.title: Revitalize Resources (Church Revitalization Funding)
sources.quote: The Revitalization Funding is for $3,000.00 per church (NAD: $1,000.00 / Union: $1,000.00 / Conference: $1,000.00).

items.name: Versacare Catalyst and Venture Grants
items.years: Catalyst: apply any time, awards April, July, October, January. Venture: portal 1 July to 31 December, awards in April

aims.text: Grants for Adventist ministries working in church community engagement, health, youth, women and children, education and humanitarian service in the NAD.
Local churches have received them, e.g. a Georgia church got $9,000 for its personal ministries.

localChurch: Catalyst $2,500 to $10,000 (best for a first grant); Venture $10,001 to $40,000; Impact (over $40,000) by invitation only.
Open to Adventist church entities and Adventist-affiliated ministries running at least two years; one Catalyst grant per organization per year.
Not funded: buildings or renovations, mission trips, salaries, debt, scholarships, start-ups. Have a budget and last year's financial statement ready.

resources.title: Catalyst Grant: what the application asks

sources.title: Our Grants
sources.quote: Catalyst applications are now accepted year-round from Seventh-day Adventist denomination entities or Seventh-day Adventist affiliated ministries and charities, with funds awarded quarterly.

sources.title: Voice of Hope $9,000 Grant
sources.quote: celebrated receiving a $9,000 grant from Versacare Foundation to further its personal ministries.

items.name: Versacare K-12 School Grants
items.years: Apply any time; awards in July and January

aims.text: Grants for church- or conference-sponsored Adventist schools, including STEM and STEAM projects.

localChurch: Up to $5,000 for schools with three classrooms or fewer; up to $10,000 for four or more.
STEM/STEAM requests need a board-approved technology plan; other requests need a board-signed letter.
A school can be funded once every three years; no building or renovation costs.

sources.title: K-12 Grants
sources.quote: K-12, STEM and STEAM applications are accepted year-round from Seventh-day Adventist Conference- or congregation-sponsored K-12, primary, middle or high schools.

items.name: ASI Convention Projects Offering
items.years: Apply by 31 December 2026 for the 2027 convention offering (every year)

aims.text: Each year ASI takes an offering at its convention and gives it to mission projects chosen ahead of time.
In 2026, 36 projects were chosen to receive grants.

localChurch: Apply by 31 December of the year before the convention (31 Dec 2026 for 2027).
The online application asks you to log in to an ASI account; call ASI (443-391-7235) to ask whether your church ministry qualifies.
Funded projects must send progress reports to ASI.

sources.title: Funding Application
sources.quote: ASI collects a special projects offering that is used to sponsor preselected ministry projects. Ministries must apply for sponsorship on or before December 31 of the prior year.

sources.title: Projects
sources.quote: The ASI Missions Inc. Board has selected 36 projects to receive grants from the offering gathered at the 2026 ASI International Convention.

items.name: Atlantic Union Revolving Fund (building loans)

aims.text: Loans for church, school and institution building projects in the Atlantic Union.

localChurch: Capital project loans for churches, schools and institutions in the Atlantic Union.
Contact the Revolving Fund office by phone or email (listed on the page).

sources.title: Atlantic Union Revolving Fund (AURF)
sources.quote: The Atlantic Union Revolving Fund (AURF) provides capital project loans to denominational churches, schools, and institutions within the Atlantic Union territory.

items.name: Columbia Union Revolving Fund (CURF) church loans

aims.text: Loans so churches can buy, build, renovate, repair or buy equipment such as sound systems.

localChurch: Borrow up to 65% of project cost or your average yearly tithe for the last three years, whichever is lower.
Board votes, fills in the CURF loan application, and sends it to the conference treasurer; the conference forwards it to CURF.
If approved, the church signs a promissory note; money is drawn as the project needs it.

sources.title: Become a Borrower of an Entity Loan
sources.quote: CURF is here to help with Entity Loans available to churches and other eligible non-education entities in the Columbia Union.

sources.title: Conference Involvement in the Loan Process
sources.quote: Entities interested in getting a CURF loan and becoming borrowers must apply through their local conference.

items.name: NPUC Revolving Fund (building loans)

aims.text: Loans for church and school construction, purchase, renovation and other capital improvements in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington.

localChurch: Get approval to apply through your conference treasurer.
Loan money can be used for construction, buying property, renovation and other capital improvements.

sources.title: Revolving Fund Forms
sources.quote: The North Pacific Union Conference Association Revolving Fund lends money to Adventist churches, schools and other denominational institutions located in the NPUC territory (Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington).

items.name: Southern Union Revolving Fund (SURF) church loans

aims.text: Low-cost loans when churches build or buy, or schools expand, across the Southern Union.

localChurch: Loans at 5.0% (rate effective 1 Feb 2026).
Ask your local conference or the Southern Union treasury to start a loan request.

sources.title: Revolving Fund
sources.quote: The purpose of SURF is to provide low-cost loans to churches and other institutions across the Southern Union Conference while providing a reasonable rate of return to investors.

items.name: Serve One More Project Fund
items.years: Applications open (no deadline posted); fall revitalization training 16-17 October 2026

aims.text: Helps churches and schools start new ways of serving their neighbors, then build bridges to deeper friendship.

localChurch: The conference pays up to 70% of the cost of a new community project and its follow-up 'bridge' steps.
Plan must meet a need named by community leaders, be new for your church or school, put members in direct contact with people, and be board-approved.
Churches in the conference revitalization track (training 16-17 Oct 2026) go to the head of the line for this funding.

sources.title: Serve One More funding application
sources.quote: Upper Columbia Conference will participate with the local church/school in up to 70% of the total cost of your project steps and bridge steps.

sources.title: Serve One More
sources.quote: The Serve One More initiative helps churches and schools across our conference discover the joy of serving their neighbors in meaningful ways.

sources.title: Church Revitalization
sources.quote: connect with a trained revitalization coach, and jump to the head of the line to receive Serve One More Community Engagement Funding.

items.name: All Things New (OneVoice27) church toolkit

aims.text: A year-long NAD outreach with ready-made social media content, training, a Desire of Ages reading plan and a sharing book.
Launched 5 Sept 2026 and runs to September 2027.

localChurch: Download the shareable presentation and reading plan to introduce it to your church board.
Use the four phases (Pray, Serve, Share, Follow Jesus) to plan the church year; ask your conference about copies of the sharing book.

resources.title: All Things New site and downloads

sources.title: All Things New
sources.quote: All Things New will support a coordinated year-long digital witness with quality content, practical training, and tools that help churches respond to interest with personal care.

sources.title: All Things New
sources.quote: The OneVoice27 initiative officially launches Sept. 5, 2026, beginning a year-long mobilization effort leading to September 2027.

items.name: Ten Days of Prayer 2027 materials
items.years: Every January; 2027 materials are already posted

aims.text: Daily prayer guides and a closing-Sabbath plan for churches to start 2027 in prayer, tied to OneVoice27.

localChurch: Download the 2027 materials and plan ten days of prayer meetings plus a closing celebration Sabbath.
Theme for 2027: All Things New: Hope Starts Here.

sources.title: Ten Days of Prayer 2027
sources.quote: Ten Days of Prayer materials were prepared by the Ministerial Association of the General Conference of Seventh-day Adventists.

items.name: New Beginnings evangelism series (free download)

aims.text: A complete lay evangelism series with presentations, sermon notes and children's series, free in many languages.

localChurch: Download the slides and notes free; works with the Discover Bible lessons.
Includes children's series (ages 4-12) and Abundant Living health presentations.

sources.title: New Beginnings
sources.quote: All materials can be downloaded free of charge. New Beginnings can also be used with the Discover Bible Lessons by Voice of Prophecy.

items.name: ASI BibleConnect (online Bible study matching)

aims.text: Trains members to give Bible studies and pairs them with people waiting to study online by Zoom.

localChurch: Members sign up to be paired with a student or to get training first.

sources.title: BibleConnect
sources.quote: ASI BibleConnect empowers Adventists to share the truth of Scripture through online Bible studies.

items.name: Safety Sabbath resources
items.years: Every year; 2026 date was 28 March (fourth Sabbath of March); watch for the 2027 topic

aims.text: Free yearly safety kit for churches: risk check, drill planning (fire, tornado, missing child, active shooter) and safety officer articles.

localChurch: Register the church on the Safety Sabbath page to get the resources.
Pick and run one drill that fits your church's biggest risk.

sources.title: Safety Sabbath
sources.quote: Each year Adventist Risk Management®, Inc. provides churches with resources to help them focus on a specific area of safety.

sources.title: Safety Sabbath
sources.quote: Register your church today to take part in Safety Sabbath® on March 28, 2026 — the fourth Sabbath of March

items.name: ARM Risk Training Center (free safety courses)

aims.text: Free online safety and risk courses for pastors, safety officers and club leaders, in English and Spanish, with certificates.

localChurch: Have your safety officer and Pathfinder/Adventurer leaders take the free courses.

sources.title: Risk Training Center
sources.quote: These courses are completely free of charge and learners will receive a certificate of completion after they finish each course.

items.name: Free wills and estate planning for members

aims.text: Local Adventist planned-giving staff help members with wills, trusts and gift plans, generally at no charge.

localChurch: Invite your conference Planned Giving office to hold a wills seminar or meet members.
Find the nearest office on willplan.us.

sources.title: Will Plan (United States)
sources.quote: The information on this website pertains to our services within the United States and are generally free of charge to members of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.

sources.title: Planned Giving and Trust Services
sources.quote: Administered locally by people who worship right beside you, our services generally are free—so every church member can effectively manage the resources God entrusts to them.

items.name: PSI help finding and writing grants

aims.text: The NAD's fundraising office helps Adventist organizations find corporate, foundation and government grants and write proposals.

localChurch: Ask your conference to connect you with PSI for grant search and proposal help (cost not stated).
PSI's five fundraising courses are on Adventist Learning Community.

sources.title: Philanthropic Service for Institutions
sources.quote: Assistance in identifying and securing corporate, foundation, and governmental grants, emphasizing their expertise in proposal writing and efficient funder identification.

items.name: Adventist Community Health Initiative (free clinics with churches)

aims.text: Helps local churches put on free medical, dental and vision clinics and health screenings for their communities.

localChurch: Contact the Lake Union Adventist Community Health department to plan a clinic or screening with your church.
Clinics offer free medical, dental and eye care to the community.

sources.title: Adventist Community Health Initiative
sources.quote: We are here to provide resources to local churches to enable them to offer medical evangelism outreach to their communities

items.name: Seeds and ACTS church-planting training
items.years: Seeds hosted by conferences through the year; Adventist pre-conference at Exponential, Orlando, 14-15 March 2027

aims.text: Two-day Seeds events and the ACTS coaching track that train members and pastors to start new groups and churches.

localChurch: Ask your conference when its next Seeds event or ACTS cohort runs.
NADEI's Adventist pre-conference at Exponential is 14-15 March 2027 (ticketed).

sources.title: Church Planting
sources.quote: Going Wide–Seeds is a two-day Equipping Experience adapted to your Conference context.

sources.title: Exponential 2027 SDA Pre Conference
sources.quote: Come and connect with like-minded people in the church planting world!

items.name: Seeds Conference 2026 (free)

aims.text: A free weekend on making disciples, missional small groups and planting churches, with kids' program and meals.

localChurch: Free, but you must register to get meals and materials.
Bring a team from your church; children's program for ages 4-12.

sources.title: Seeds Conference 2026
sources.quote: Gather with us at Seeds, Nov. 6-7 at Kirkland SDA Church!

sources.title: Washington Seeds 2026
sources.quote: You must register (FREE) to receive meals and materials.
